evidence.title: Technical data sheet - TL-5 tank sealing compound
evidence.claim: Nitrogen filling for TL-5 is required because water reacts with isocyanate to form CO2 gas (2021).
evidence.quote: water reacts with isocyanate and forms CO2. Packed in 5 L cans under dry nitrogen

evidence.title: Change request CR-2005-009
evidence.claim: Moisture ingress caused pressure build-up in TL-5 cans, leading to the implementation of a nitrogen blanket (2005).
evidence.quote: Reason: IR-2005-011 (pressure build-up in cans from moisture ingress).

evidence.title: DEVIATION REPORT DR-2002-008
evidence.claim: In 2002, condensation in empty cans from Latte Brunetti caused rust spots and gelled skins in TL-5 product.
evidence.quote: rust spots and gelled skins inside cans. Empty cans from Latte Brunetti are stored outdoors under a tarpaulin

evidence.title: Incident report IR-2005-011
evidence.claim: In 2005, humid air entering the D-4 headspace caused CO2 production and a can lid to blow off.
evidence.quote: humid summer air was drawn into the D-4 headspace during the isocyanate addition; the water reacted with isocyanate and produced CO2

evidence.title: Minutes - cost review, 15 October 2019
evidence.claim: In 2019, the nitrogen blanket was maintained because MDI prepolymer reacts with moisture, causing safety-critical blown lids.
evidence.quote: Keep: the MDI prepolymer still reacts with moisture in air and blown lids are a safety issue.

evidence.title: Supplier qualification SQ-2017-004 - Imballaggi Corvino S.r.l.
evidence.claim: In October 2017, Imballaggi Corvino S.r.l. replaced Latte Brunetti as the supplier of 5 L tinplate cans.

verdict.process_name: TL-5 tank sealing compound (1K moisture-cure polyurethane)
verdict.instruction: Fill 5 L cans under dry nitrogen and seal.
verdict.reason: The step prevents moisture ingress which causes CO2 production and pressure build-up, leading to safety-critical blown lids (E4, E6, E7). While the original supplier causing condensation issues was replaced (E8), the chemical reaction between MDI prepolymer and moisture remains a safety hazard (E7).
